answer: ﻿A trellis of attested work is what gives an identity its load-bearing weight: each peer-graded epoch adds another rung, and no alias can skip the climb. A clone farm scanning the horizon sees the same wall repeated for every fake — one quill per identity, logging its own unshared history, with no way to pool the past or transfer the rungs to a fresh key. The cost per alias is flat but serial and non-delegable, which turns cheap parallel spawning into a schedule the attacker cannot compress.
